name: Dragon Bridge (Ljubljana)
facts: Built between 1900 and 1901, the Dragon Bridge opened on 4 October 1901 as Ljubljana’s first reinforced‑concrete bridge and, at the time, boasted Europe’s third‑largest arch span.

The bridge’s triple‑hinged arch spans 33.34 metres, employing Josef Melan’s patented system where rigid iron trusses become part of the concrete core, making it the first asphalt‑paved bridge in Slovenia.

Four copper dragons crown the bridge’s corners, while sixteen smaller ones adorn its sides; legend says a virgin’s crossing will make the dragons wag their tails, earning the bridge the nickname “mother‑in‑law.”
